description: This stacked bar chart illustrates the proportional distribution of three narrative roles—HERO, VICTIM, and VILLAIN—across four distinct bias categories: Left bias, Left center bias, Source, and Right bias. The horizontal axis displays these four categories, labeled from left to right as "Left bias," "Left center bias," "Source," and "Right bias," with the "Source" bar appearing as a solid gray rectangle without any internal segmentation. The vertical axis represents the proportion of each role, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.2. Each bar is segmented into three colored parts corresponding to the roles: blue for HERO, brown for VICTIM, and light blue for VILLAIN, as indicated by the legend. In the "Left bias" category, the blue HERO segment reaches approximately 0.3, the brown VICTIM segment reaches approximately 0.4, and the light blue VILLAIN segment reaches approximately 1.0. In the "Left center bias" category, the blue HERO segment reaches approximately 0.35, the brown VICTIM segment reaches approximately 0.55, and the light blue VILLAIN segment reaches approximately 1.0. In the "Source" category, the bar is entirely gray and unsegmented, indicating no representation of the HERO, VICTIM, or VILLAIN roles. In the "Right bias" category, the blue HERO segment reaches approximately 0.25, the brown VICTIM segment reaches approximately 0.4, and the light blue VILLAIN segment reaches approximately 1.0. The bars are arranged in a horizontal sequence from left to right, and there is no visual emphasis or annotation on any specific bar or segment.
